faqs.a: Many electrical jobs require a permit and inspection, including new circuits, service or panel upgrades, and many generator and EV charger installations. Requirements differ between the City of Hagerstown and unincorporated Washington County, so a licensed electrician can confirm what applies to your project and typically pulls the permit for you.
faqs.q: Do I need a permit for electrical work in Hagerstown or Washington County?

faqs.a: Common signs include breakers that trip often, lights that dim when large appliances start, a panel that feels warm or buzzes, outlets that stop working, and older panels from brands with known safety issues. Adding an EV charger, heat pump, or home addition can also require more capacity. A load calculation from a licensed electrician will show whether an upgrade is needed.
faqs.q: How do I know if my home needs an electrical panel upgrade?

faqs.a: In many cases, yes. The electrician will first check your panel's capacity and the condition of the wiring, then size the circuit for the charger. If the service is too small, a panel or service upgrade may be needed before installation. A permit and inspection are usually required.
faqs.q: Can you install an EV charger in an older home?

faqs.a: Maryland requires electrical contractors to be licensed, and homeowners should confirm the license and insurance before any work begins. You can verify a Maryland electrical license through the Maryland State Board of Master Electricians, and ask for proof of general liability and workers' compensation coverage.
